external_sources.title: HSE Health and safety checklist for classrooms
external_sources.supports: The ordinary classroom checklist excludes specialist D&T facilities. Staff must use activity-appropriate risk assessment and management for practical work.

external_sources.title: Science Buddies Build the Best Paper Bridge
external_sources.supports: A flat paper sheet can be folded into a channel for a model bridge. The local 20 by 8 cm card plan is an authored choice. This pack covers identification and marking out only; building and testing occur in later scheme weeks.

evidence.description: Individual material and tool identification, a sample observation and a hazard with a safe action; record actual support and response to feedback.

routes.Supported: Supported: start with A, B, C and D.
routes.Independent: Independent: sort all six and give a use.
routes.Aspire: Aspire: explain a material choice for a model.

vocab.definition: What we use to make something.
An item that helps us do a task.
Parts arranged to hold a shape or load.

cases.text: Paper: a thin sheet for a sketch or model.
cases.fact: Paper is used to make or draw on.
cases.next_step: Bend a small sample gently. Describe what you notice.
cases.staff_note: Compare paper and card samples of the same size. Accept observations of the actual samples; do not assume every card is stiffer.

cases.text: Card: a sheet for a small model.
cases.fact: Card is used to form the model.
cases.next_step: Check the edge before gently bending the sample.
cases.staff_note: Use clean, dry card with no staples or rough edges. No folding or building of the final blank today.

cases.text: Ruler: a tool with a scale.
cases.fact: It measures length and guides a straight line.
cases.next_step: Lay it flat. Find the zero mark.
cases.staff_note: Zero on the scale may not be the physical end of the ruler. Use a clear centimetre scale.

cases.text: Pencil: a tool that leaves a mark.
cases.fact: It draws lines and marks points.
cases.next_step: Keep it on the mat when it is not in use.
cases.staff_note: Do not wave or throw pencils. Use an appropriate grip or larger pencil if needed.

cases.text: Scissors: a tool for cutting. Use the picture today.
cases.next_step: Ask the adult before any cutting task.
cases.staff_note: Identification only in this pack. No pupil cutting. Staff prepare blanks beforehand under local procedures.

cases.text: Tape: a material used to join parts.
cases.next_step: Use only a staff-prepared sample today.
cases.staff_note: Use a short piece on a backing card; no live dispenser or assembly is needed.

Accept the observed result. A hazard must pair with a suitable action, for example sharp staple: stop and tell staff. Do not credit a copied model as an independent observation.

Lundy moments

Space: a calm place and accessible materials. Voice: a choice or request for help. Audience: the adult listens, checks and replies. Influence: record the requested support or next task and the change made.
Speaking listening and writing

Private help and reflection

Offer a quiet help request or an observation alternative. If a concern is disclosed, listen calmly, follow local safeguarding procedures and keep that record separate from lesson evidence. Do not promise secrecy.

Materials: paper, card or tape. Tools: ruler, pencil or scissors. A ruler measures/guides a straight line; a pencil marks; scissors cut. Compare equal-size paper and card samples by gentle bending. Accept the observed result. A hazard must pair with a suitable action, for example sharp staple: stop and tell staff. Do not credit a copied model as an independent observation.
Feedback and safe teaching
Card A: Compare paper and card samples of the same size. Accept observations of the actual samples; do not assume every card is stiffer.
Card B: Use clean, dry card with no staples or rough edges. No folding or building of the final blank today.
Card C: Zero on the scale may not be the physical end of the ruler. Use a clear centimetre scale.
Card D: Do not wave or throw pencils. Use an appropriate grip or larger pencil if needed.
Card E: Identification only in this pack. No pupil cutting. Staff prepare blanks beforehand under local procedures.
Card F: Use a short piece on a backing card; no live dispenser or assembly is needed.
Common misunderstandings

A material becomes part of an item; a tool helps do the work. The same object may serve different purposes in other contexts. Card is not always stiffer than every kind of paper: compare the actual equal-size samples. Safe work means controlling risks, not claiming that nothing can go wrong.
